text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and can not vouch for their accuracy.
- Public transport drivers have rejected new fares introduced by the United Transport and Taxis Association to counter recent fuel price hikes, saying they would push them out of business.
- The farmers union warned that Zambia would realise poor crop yields next year because of the late arrival of inputs in some farming communities.
- Clinics in prisons across the country have run out of drugs, increasing the chances of inmates escaping when being taken to hospitals.

- Police have summoned opposition leader Dean Mungomba for questioning. Mungomba has been sought after by police since late November, when he called for an armed insurrection against the government, which he claimed rigged general elections.
